lesson.description: Learn the key ideas for both sides in the sharp Benko Gambit.

{How can Black ensure that White won't be able to castle?} 7... Bxf1 {[%wrong
There's a much stronger move. Try again and look for a way to stop White from
castling.] [%hint Trade bishops.] White must play Kxf1 to win back the piece
and must lose the right to castle. This is a key idea in the Benko when White
advances the e-pawn.} *

{How should White clear a safe square for the king?} 9. g3 {[%wrong There's a
better option. Try again and look for a useful pawn move.] [%hint Clear a
square for your king to evacuate the first rank.]} (9. a4 $5 {This is
reasonable, but it's more popular to advance a kingside pawn to allow a safer
square for your king. How should you do it?}) (9. Nf3 $5 {This is reasonable,
but it's more popular to advance a pawn to allow a safer square for your king.
How should you do it?}) (9. f4 $2 Bg7 {It makes sense to control the center,
but this exposes the white king. Try to find a better kingside pawn move.}) (9.
f3 $2 Bg7 {White may end up weak on the dark squares. Try again and look for a
better pawn move.}) (9. g4 $2 Bg7 {There's a safer square for this pawn. Try
to find it.}) 9... Bg7 {Nice move! How can you continue to "castle by hand?"}
10. Kg2 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a strong king
move.] [%hint Hide your king on the g-file.] Well played! White's king is
relatively safe on the kingside, although Black still has an initiative on the
queenside.} (10. a4 $5 {This is reasonable, but most players prefer to bring
the king off of the back rank. How can you do it?}) (10. Nf3 $5 {This is
reasonable, but most players prefer to bring the king off of the back rank.
How can you do it?}) (10. Ke2 $2 {It's better to bring your king away from the
center. Try again and look for a stronger king move.}) *

{How should Black recapture after White's dxe6 in the Blumenfeld Gambit?} 5...
fxe6 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a strong capture.
] [%hint Recapture without allowing a queen trade.]} (5... dxe6 $2 6. Qxd8+ {
White enters an endgame and then captures on b5. Try again and look for a
stronger capture.}) (5... bxc4 $2 6. exf7+ {Black's king is exposed and White
is doing well. Try again and look for a stronger capture.}) 6. cxb5 {Great
move! How can Black dominate the center?} d5 {[%wrong There's a stronger
option. Try again and look for a good pawn advance.] [%hint Control the center
with a third pawn.] Well played! Both sides have chances, although Alexander
Alekhine went on to win a famous game in Tarrasch - Alekhine, 1922.} (6... Be7
$2 7. Bf4 {Black doesn't have enough compensation for the sacrificed pawn. Try
again and look for a way to dominate the center.}) (6... Bb7 $2 7. Nc3 {
Black doesn't have enough compensation for the sacrificed pawn. Try again and
look for a way to dominate the center.}) (6... a6 $2 7. e3 {In the Blumenfeld
Gambit, Black is better off controlling the center instead of sacrificing the
a-pawn. Try again and look for a better pawn move.}) *

{White wants to prepare b3 and Bb2, without allowing a pin on the long
diagonal. How can you do it?} 11. Rb1 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try to
find it and check the hint if you're stuck.] [%hint Move your a1 rook off of
the long diagonal.] Great job! This prophylactic move gives White the chance
to play b3 and achieve a good position.} (11. Qc2 $5 {This is a good move, but
we're looking to prepare the b3 advance. How should you do it?}) (11. Bf4 $5 {
This is a good move, but we're looking to prepare the b3 advance. How should

} 9. Nxd5 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try again and look for a precise
capture.] [%hint Capture a piece and make a discovery against the black queen.]
} Qxb5 {Black only wins back the piece for a moment. How should White win

winning fork.] [%hint Fork three black pieces with your knight.]} Kd8 {A great
shot! What's next?} 11. Nxb5 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try again and
look for a good capture.] [%hint Capture the queen.] Well done!} *

{How can Black win back the sacrificed pawn?} 14... Bxc3 {[%wrong There's a
better option. Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Capture the
defender of the a2-pawn.]} (14... c4 $2 15. Qd2 {There's a better option. Try
again and look for a way to win back the sacrificed pawn.}) (14... Qd7 $2 15.
h3 {There's a better option. Try again and look for a way to win back the
sacrificed pawn.}) 15. Bxc3 {Good choice! What's next?} Rxa2 {[%wrong There's
a better option. Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Capture an
undefended pawn.] Good work! White's bishop pair offers a small advantage, but
Black has won back the pawn and isolated the weak pawn on b3.} *

{How did GM Hikaru Nakamura keep a material advantage?} 28. Nd1 {[%wrong
There's a better option. Try again and look for a strong threat.] [%hint
Attack the black bishop with another piece.]} (28. Nc2 $5 {This is reasonable,
but Nakamura preferred to target the black bishop. What did he play?}) 28...
Nxb3 {Good choice! How can you regain a material advantage?} 29. Nxc3 {[%wrong
There's a better option. Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Find
a good capture.]} bxc3 {Nice move! What's next?} 30. Rxc3 {[%wrong There's a
better option. Try again and look for a good capture?] [%hint Capture a pawn.]}
(30. Rc8+ $5 {This is OK, but why not capture something right away?}) 30... Nc5
{Well played! How can you keep your extra pawn?} 31. Ra3 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try again and look for a way to save your passed pawn.] [%hint
Defend a5 with your rook.] Well played! White eventually converted the extra
pawn into a win in Nakamura - Bologan, 2012.} *

{How did GM Sam Shankland start a combination to win back material after his
sacrifice in the opening?} 10... Nxe4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try
again and look for a strong sacrifice.] [%hint Sacrifice a piece to distract a
defender of the d5-pawn.]} (10... exd5 $2 11. Nxd5 {White keeps a material
edge and a good position. Try again and look for a stronger capture.}) (10...
Be7 $2 11. Nf3 {White keeps an extra pawn and a good position. Try again and
look for a strong capture.}) 11. Nxe4 {Great choice! How can you justify the
piece sacrifice?} Bxd5 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for
a strong capture.] [%hint Capture a pawn and target the white queen.] Great
work! You can continue the combination from Zhai - Shankland, 2019 in the next
challenge.} (11... exd5 $2 12. Ng3 {White keeps an extra piece and Black is in
trouble. Try again and look for a stronger capture.}) *

preferred to attack the e4-knight with a pawn. How did he do it?}) (12... Bxe4
$2 13. Qxe4 {After Qxb5 and Qxa8 White wins material. Try again and look for a
strong threat.}) 13. Ng3 {Great move! What's next?} Bxg2 {[%wrong White keeps
a material advantage. Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Capture

a strong capture. What was his idea?}) 14. N1e2 {Nice work! What should you

capture.] [%hint Capture an undefended piece.] Well done! Black went on to win
